blockingFindings.claim: Planning to win the second spade unnecessarily preserves defensive communication.
blockingFindings.evidence: If West has five spades and East three plus the diamond ace, taking the second spade leaves East a spade to return after winning DA. West can then cash three spades: four spade tricks plus DA defeat 3NT. Ducking twice instead exhausts East's spades. This preserves the planned nine winners and dummy's heart entry; a 4–4 spade break still concedes only three spades plus DA.
blockingFindings.requestedChange: Keep S7, but plan to duck two spade rounds before taking SA if spades continue. Retain reassessment for defensive switches.
